title: coons_inset_faces: merge inner edges across selected adjacent cage faces (shared-edge bridging)
description:
Today coons_inset_faces emits 1 inner quad + 4 side quads per selected face, unconditionally, with fresh inner verts per face (see CoonsInsetFacesNode.java pass 1 & 2). When two or more selected cage faces share an edge, their inner quads are topologically disjoint: each inner quad's verts are brand-new, the shared cage edge ends up with two side quads (one from each face, one per winding direction), and there is no edge-adjacency between the inner quads themselves. Downstream coons_extrude_mesh(selection=generated, region=true) — even with the MESH-43 connected-component fix — sees each inner quad as its own component and extrudes them independently. That produces cheese-grater on every inset-then-extrude feature in the coons_cage technique (eye sockets, nasal cavity carves, cheekbone depressions — all of them). This is the bottleneck blocking the whole coons_cage workflow from producing smooth carved features.

Fix direction: when cage edge e has two selected incident faces A and B, drop both side quads on e, merge the 2 inner-edge verts from each face into shared verts along e, and let the inner quads become edge-adjacent directly. A contiguous selected region of cage faces should produce ONE connected inner patch, whose perimeter follows the selection boundary. At cage corners where 3+ selected faces meet, the corresponding inner verts (one per face near that cage corner) must be merged as well.

CRITICAL (per user note): merged inner vertices MUST lie on the Coons surface. That is the whole point of the 'coons_' prefix — plain inset_faces places verts on flat cage lerps, coons_inset_faces places them on the bezier-handled Coons surface. When two face-local Coons evaluations at their respective (t, ...) parameters produce nearby-but-not-identical world positions for what should be the same merged vertex, the merged position must either (a) be evaluated via a shared cage-edge-aware parameterization so both faces agree by construction, or (b) be projected back onto the Coons surface after merging. Naive midpoint averaging between two face-local samples is NOT acceptable — it drifts off the surface and reintroduces the 'cheese grater' artifact that coons_inset_faces exists to prevent.
definition-of-done: 1. When two or more selected cage faces share an edge, coons_inset_faces emits exactly one shared pair of inner verts along that cage edge (not one pair per face). At corners where N>=3 selected faces meet, the N face-local near-corner inner verts merge into one. 2. The resulting inner quads within a single selection-connected-component are edge-adjacent through their shared inner edges. 3. All merged inner verts lie on the Coons surface (assert with a test that samples distance-to-surface and tolerates < 1e-4 of mesh extent). 4. Side quads on shared edges between two selected faces are NOT emitted (the inner quads are directly bridged). Side quads are only emitted on selection-boundary cage edges. 5. coons_extrude_mesh(selection=inset.generated, region=true) downstream produces one extruded region per selection-connected-component of the original cage selection (not per inner face). 6. Regression test: pre-fix and post-fix face counts and vertex counts on a 2x1 grid with both faces selected differ predictably; post-fix inner quads share 2 verts on the shared edge. 7. The generated output mask is the UNION of inner faces (merged or not), matching downstream selection expectations.
testing-plan: 1. Unit: 3x3 grid, select faces 0+1 (edge adjacent). Assert output has 1 shared pair of inner verts on their common edge (fewer total verts than pre-fix). 2. Unit: 2x2 grid, select all 4 faces (share a central corner). Assert the 4 face-local near-center inner verts merge into 1 shared vert. 3. Unit: for each merged inner vert, sample Coons surface on one of the source faces and assert |v - S(u, v)| < 1e-4 * mesh_extent. 4. Integration: select_by_distance picks 2 edge-adjacent cage faces → coons_inset_faces → coons_extrude_mesh(selection=generated, region=true). Assert the extrude output has 1 connected component (not 2). 5. Re-run the skull voyage-batch run from VOYAGE-46/47 and check whether eye-socket, nasal cavity, and brow ridge features render smoothly vs cheese-grater — target similarity 68.7% → 80%+.
